derived_actionables.text: Add a static per-role latency term to model selection: T_hat(role) = nominal per-role TPOT x predicted output length, reusing the existing baseline_tps_by_role config, which is currently only reward-side. Expose it as a weight on the selection score. A/B it against current selection in a load sweep that includes saturating the latency-preferred role, measuring E2E, TTFT and realized quality. Wire the run's write side into the belief kernel as a claim tuple (scripts/vidya/adapters/README.md).

Add a saturation guard to selection: when a role's slots are all busy (orchestrator dispatch ledger / admission gate; cross-check llamacpp:requests_deferred > 0), add the expected wait to that role's T_hat, using dead reckoning from in-flight dispatches plus predicted lengths. Do NOT add a second telemetry poller or occupancy model.
Keep model selection inside the orchestrator behind /v1. The harness sends role/intent hints only (x_force_role, x_orchestrator_role) and gets no per-model capacity or latency surface to route on.
Build an HW-Router-style learned live latency predictor, or an SFS engine-snapshot simulator, for role selection.

Record the llama-server signal map in the contention rider. HW-Router's running and waiting counts map to llamacpp:requests_processing and requests_deferred (/metrics, which needs --metrics). KV-cache usage has NO analogue: KV is preallocated per slot at launch; the nearest is per-slot fullness from /slots n_prompt_tokens + n_decoded vs n_ctx. TTFT/TPOT averages have to come from counter deltas (prompt_seconds_total/prompt_tokens_total excludes queue wait); the prompt_tokens_seconds and predicted_tokens_seconds gauges are effectively lifetime averages in v10, because metrics_reset_bucket is never set true. RouteBalance's pending decode tokens d_i are not exposed (n_remain is -1 without n_predict). SFS's resident prefill is partly exposed: v10 /slots emits n_prompt_tokens, n_prompt_tokens_processed and n_prompt_tokens_cache, while deferred-request lengths are not exposed.
Make sure any per-request routing classifier on the /v1 hot path is amortised or batched, and never a serial per-request forward that saturates under concurrent fan-out.

Derive the chat-door 503 Retry-After from live slot/queue state (contention gate + admission queue) instead of the constants 5/10/30 s (src/api/__init__.py:388-407, :418; src/api/routes/chat.py:319-321). Also emit retry-after-ms, which pinned OpenCode reads first (session/retry.ts:51-56). Budget for RETRY_MAX_RETRIES=5: after 5 failures the turn fails, so a long queue should hold the request rather than bounce it.

On the MCP control door, while orchestrator_chat waits for a slot, send notifications/progress (monotone progress plus a message such as "queued: position N, est. S s") to keep the call alive. Set an explicit OpenCode mcp timeout or experimental.mcp_timeout, since the SDK default is 60000 ms and OpenCode resets it only on progress. Note that OpenCode discards the progress message, so this is a keep-alive and not a visible signal. Any user-visible capacity text must go in the tool result.

In the HS-3 row, record that ACP providers/set (Draft, unstable_llm_providers) does NOT meet the "ACP gains inference-routing semantics" trigger: it is process-scoped endpoint redirection that duplicates the opencode.jsonc baseURL. Also record that pinned OpenCode does not implement it. Keep HS-3 not-triggered, with no checkbox change.
Adopt the MCP Tasks extension for orchestrator_* tools (FastMCP 4.x + fastmcp-tasks), returning a task handle when no slot is free.
Emit an ACP-shaped usage_update analogue (context + cost) from the Orch in x_orchestrator_metadata (the Stage-1 recommended action).

If a harness->Orch priority hint is ever added to the chat door, name its typed x_* fields after MCP's costPriority/speedPriority/intelligencePriority (0-1, advisory, Orch makes the final choice). Cite them as borrowed vocabulary, not as a live MCP standard.
Run the orchestrator as an ACP proxy/conductor between an editor and OpenCode.

/v1 front door: accept session identity from headers as a fallback when the x_session_id body key is absent. Order: body x_session_id, then x-dynamo-session-id, then OpenCode X-Session-Id. Also record parent_session_id from x-dynamo-parent-session-id or x-parent-session-id. Make the v1_client_session_guard check the header before returning 422. Unit-test the precedence and a child `task` request that carries x-parent-session-id.

Slot record: name three per-slot capacity fields in proposal-003 semantics. queued comes from llamacpp:requests_deferred, running from llamacpp:requests_processing, and kv_occupancy is derived from GET /slots (sum of n_prompt_tokens+n_decoded over processing slots / sum of n_ctx). Flag kv_occupancy as not meaningful for O(1)-KV GDN-hybrid residents. Carry EPYC-only fields beside them: device_class (cpu|gpu), numa_node/cpuset, residency state including UNKNOWN, co-tenant/contention count, and measured prompt/predicted tokens-per-second.
Front the orchestrator with a GAIE/llm-d Endpoint Picker (ext-proc) consuming proposal-003 gauges from llama-server slots.
Rename or alias the orchestrator's x_* override keys to Dynamo's nvext.agent_hints names so SDKs that emit them work unchanged.

Within-role replica choice: record Dynamo's cost shape as the reference load term. It is scaled uncached-prefill blocks + active decode blocks + optional per-active-request weight, with softmax temperature for spread. Note that the prefix-overlap term needs per-slot prefix state, and llama-server offers only post-hoc n_prompt_tokens_cache rather than KV events.

Record intake-1810's intra-node GPU-prefill / CPU-decode disaggregation (one shared DRAM weight copy; <2K chunked, long -> GPU streaming, decode batched to a target) as the design prior in numa-prefill-decode-disaggregation.md. In the same edit, correct the handoff's topology premise at :14 and :34: the host is 1 socket / NPS4 per lscpu, so there is no xGMI inter-socket KV path.

Add a prefill-length routing rule candidate to heterogeneous-slot-fabric-residency.md. For an over-HBM MoE whose weights are DRAM-resident, route a prefill to a GPU streaming path only when predicted CPU prefill time exceeds streamed_bytes / 28.9 GB/s (34.6 ms per GB, our measured H2D). Replace the '~26 GB/s' at :77 with the measured 28.89 GB/s receipt.

Measure CPU prefill tok/s vs prompt length (1K-32K) for the largest over-HBM MoE on the production recipe. In the same window, measure llama.cpp's -cmoe op-offload prefill (which already streams CPU-resident experts to the MI210 for ubatch>=32) so the SLP-style crossover for our host becomes a measured number.

In the fable5 OD-A rider: tick F3 (:242) citing the 2026-08-03 H2D/D2H receipt (gpu-acceleration-path.md:330); correct :220-221 (#1612 was answered by a collaborator on 2025-11-15); and add that at c40722bf the AVX-512 native backends exist in source, overturning intake-923's 'no AVX-512-native MoE operator family' (research/intake_index.yaml:54822).

OD-A decision package framing: the kt-kernel CPU half is source-portable to Zen 5 (BF16/FP8/RAWINT4/LLAMAFILE without AMX), its prefill benefit is AMX-dependent in the paper, and the GPU half is CUDA-packaged with an untested ROCm option. Keep R-A7 F1 (per-split overlap ceiling under static -cmoe) as the gate before any runtime or kernel work.

Optional OD-A evidence: a build-only check of kt-kernel on the host (CPUINFER_CPU_INSTRUCT=NATIVE, CPUINFER_USE_ROCM=1, in an isolated venv under /mnt/raid0/llm/tmp) that records __cpu_variant__ / __fp8_kernel__ / __rawint4_kernel__. No inference.

Supersede the pre-BIOS DRAM bandwidth rows (cpu-decode-roofline-program.md:147-150, and wiki/hardware-optimization.md:99 '220 GB/s ceiling') with the post-2026-09-21 artifacts (read-sum t=96 446.8 / 449.4 GB/s; 83% of 537.6 theoretical).
Adopt or port 1810's SLP/DSLP implementation.

Fill the N-dwell swap cost C per (model, MI210) from a hot-page-cache load on the PRODUCTION kernel store (v10). Use a decomposed timer: process start -> 'load_model' -> 'model loaded' -> first token, read from llama-server stderr and emitted with the effective config. Fit C = a + size/b per the fixed-penalty form, and write it into the model capability record. Cold/post-reboot C stays gated on the operator protocol per mi210-big-model-and-acceleration-roadmap.md:296.

Record an explicit DECLINE of token/step-level GPU model multiplexing (Aegaeon-style) for the llama-server fabric. Reason: it is mid-decode preemption (axiom 4). It needs engine internals llama-server lacks: in-process component reuse, host KV pool, IPC-event KV sync, and in-flight slot KV save (server-context.cpp:2593-2596 defers while processing). Prefetch-hiding needs VRAM for two models' weights beyond the 58 GB 2-resident set. Revisit only if an experimental-branch llama-server gains cooperative decode preemption (within-role-placement-state-machine.md:31).

Add a Layer-3 residency policy prior: when a swap to model B is fired, admit queued and tracked B-eligible sessions as a group, bounded like Aegaeon's MAX_GPSIZE, before any swap back. This amortizes C over a group, and all of it happens at turn boundaries under the existing drain protocol.
Add 'swap cost C (hot page cache)' and 'partial-offload (-ngl < all) throughput curve' as fields of the per-model capability card.
Do not import 2605.19593's absolute reload seconds (2.6-7.3 s) or its '~2% overhead' into any EPYC cost model or dwell calculation.

Extend the "(Z) Guard the prefix-stability assumption" row so it also covers any shared-notes or blackboard block injected into delegated or REPL-worker prompts. The block must be rendered append-only and byte-identical across viewers, and placed before any per-worker, per-step or tools content. Measure reuse with llama-server /slots cache_n, alongside the existing repl-turn-efficiency.md:159 measurement. DeLM's own released prompts break all three conditions, which is the failure mode to guard against.

When the D-d curation layer (annotate/pin) is designed, specify an admission gate for shared or pinned notes. Use a deterministic grounding check first: the cited span must appear verbatim, and a PATCH-type note must reference a run that actually happened. Only then add an optional cheap-model (worker-tier) semantic check. Never route admission to the architect.
Stage-1 recommended action: prototype a DeLM-style verified shared context plus a task queue as a REPL-session mode in which idle CPU/GPU slots claim subtasks.
Add a flat, equal-rank RLM-worker arm with a verified shared-notes layer (DeLM+RLM) to the REPL scaffold A/Bs.
